query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Systematic variation of elemental composition in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA through controlled experiments will reveal the effects of changing the percentage of elements on mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy (HEA) with a uniform microstructure
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of elemental composition by adjusting the percentage of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr in the alloy
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted at room temperature, under controlled atmosphere, and on samples with a consistent processing history and minimal impurities
generation.structural_mediator: Grain size and phase distribution, which affect the yield strength of the alloy through the Hall-Petch relationship and precipitation hardening mechanisms
generation.mechanism: Changes in elemental composition alter the grain size and phase distribution, which in turn affect the mechanical properties of the alloy, as supported by existing literature on HEAs (e.g., [insert reference IDs if provided])
generation.predicted_outcome: A 10% increase in the percentage of Hf will result in a 15% increase in yield strength (from 1000 MPa to 1150 MPa) relative to the baseline composition, based on theoretical considerations of solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening
generation.baseline: HfNbTaTiZr-HEA with equal atomic percentages of each element (20% Hf, 20% Nb, 20% Ta, 20% Ti, 20% Zr)
generation.boundary: Compositional variations between 5% and 15% of the baseline composition
generation.uncertainty: The actual relationship between elemental composition and mechanical properties may be more complex than predicted, and additional factors such as processing history or impurities could influence the outcome

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with systematic variation of elemental composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength in the control experiment (with no change in Hf percentage) is not within 5% of the baseline yield strength (1000 MPa), or if the yield strength does not increase by at least 10% (to 1100 MPa) with a 10% increase in Hf percentage, the hypothesis is falsified
